cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Backward and forward integration within a single site cluster: the Company describes itself as an integrated iron and steel manufacturing company operating two integrated divisions - a Steel Melting Shop (SMS) and Foundry Division and a Rolling Mill Division. The SMS runs 12 MT fully digital medium-frequency induction furnaces in twin-shell configuration with secondary metallurgy via ladle refining furnace (LRF) and vacuum degassing (VD); the foundry has an in-house engineering and pattern development unit, continuous sand mixers, mechanised fettling via automatic shakeout, a sand reclamation plant, shot blasting and automatic paint booths; downstream are heat treatment furnaces, machine shops (>100,000 sq ft covered, CNC lathes, boring machines, roll grinding, VTL/CNC VTL, plano and CNC vertical milling) and rolling mills. Manufacturing and machining processes are described as overlapping and fungible, so the available (installed) capacity of the SMS and Foundry Division can vary with the product mix being run. Upstream, raw material (scrap, ingots, ferro alloys) is procured directly from domestic manufacturers and international suppliers without middlemen, on purchase orders rather than long term contracts; internally generated scrap is re-melted and recycled. Downstream, the Company sells directly through its in-house sales team, keeping middle-men and agents out of the sales process because products are highly customised and engineered; orders are purchase-order based with customer projections used for production planning, and long term contracts are generally avoided due to steel price volatility. Utilities: a 66 KvA sub-station, grid power from the Punjab State Electricity Board, ground water, and around 2 MW of installed rooftop solar. Corporate structure was consolidated through a Scheme of Amalgamation (NCLT Chandigarh order dated August 22, 2024) merging Belco Special Steels Private Limited (now the Rolling Mill Division) and Parkash Multimetals Private Limited (now part of the SMS and Foundry Division) into the Company.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Revenue from the top 10 customers was Rs 2,029.21 million, Rs 2,027.16 million and Rs 1,686.51 million (38.00%, 39.91% and 37.81% of revenue from operations) in Fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024, with the largest single customer at 6.96% in Fiscal 2026. The Company does not enter into long term contracts and its business is based on purchase orders, so demand can fall away at short notice.
- Cost of material consumed - primarily scrap and ferro alloys sourced domestically and internationally - was 61.02%, 60.78% and 68.62% of total expenses in Fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024. There are no long-term supply agreements with third party suppliers, and steel pricing is subject to market demand, volatility and economic conditions.
- Net working capital was Rs 1,924.50 million as at March 31, 2026 (132 working capital days) versus Rs 1,453.68 million (104 days) at March 31, 2025 and Rs 1,196.40 million (98 days) at March 31, 2024, with inventory days rising from 34 to 42 to 57. Sanctioned working capital facilities were Rs 691.03 million as on May 31, 2026 with Rs 94.36 million outstanding.
- Alloy steel products, metal rolls and engineering castings cumulatively contributed more than 90.00% of revenue from operations in each of Fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024 (91.70%, 93.14% and 94.29% from sale of customised products), so a downturn in any one of these segments is material.
- All manufacturing operations - and the Upcoming Manufacturing Facility - are located in Mandi Gobindgarh, Punjab, exposing the Company to concentrated regional, regulatory, labour and natural-event risk.
- Sales to customers in India were Rs 4,860.47 million, Rs 4,859.33 million and Rs 4,245.17 million (91.02%, 95.67% and 95.17% of revenue from operations) in Fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024. Domestic sub-total was essentially flat between Fiscal 2025 and Fiscal 2026; growth came from exports.
- Construction of the Upcoming Manufacturing Facility has only recently commenced and its completion and operation are contingent on obtaining various approvals; delays could cause cost and time overruns. The Company has not yet placed orders for the capital expenditure equipment and machinery to be funded from the Net Proceeds, and the fund requirements have not been appraised by any bank or financial institution.
- The Order Book was Rs 1,182.87 million as on March 31, 2026 (Rs 930.03 million and Rs 855.45 million at the two prior year ends) and Rs 1,785.69 million as of May 31, 2026, but the Company states that current order book value is not necessarily indicative of future growth and some orders may be modified or cancelled.
